name: Kelp Forest
desc: A giant-kelp forest running its conveyor — the meristem at each blade's base extrudes tissue continuously while the distal tip erodes away, so corrugations stream forever up the blades and vanish at their ends; gas bladders float the stipes into a flattened surface canopy, wave surge rolls the whole forest with an orbital motion that dies away with depth, and new sporophytes recruit on the rock as old ones let go and wash out of frame.

energy.doc: surge amplitude + blade flap + how fast the conveyor extrudes and the forest turns over

density.doc: how many stipes make up the forest (3 at 0 -> 16 at 1) and how thick the marine snow is

scale.doc: stipe and blade size vs frame (2.2 = swimming inside one plant)

hue.doc: blade hue in the plate/xray/sonar looks (cyanotype is monochrome by construction)

x.doc: which part of the forest the frame is looking at

y.doc: vertical placement of the surface and the rocky bottom

surge.doc: wave energy — a glassy calm at 0, a rolling groundswell at 1

style.doc: aesthetic — Atkins' British Algae photogram (pale mass on Prussian blue); chromolithograph plate w/ ink line and modelled blades; additive translucent radiograph; false-colour acoustic echogram

seed.doc: seeds recruitment sites, depth planes, blade counts and life spans

alpha.doc: opacity of the forest over the water column
